## What you can call

| method | route | scopes | idempotent | timeout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeOrder` | `POST /v1/tenants/{tenantId}/orders` | — | yes | 5000ms |
| `getOrder` ⚠️ | `GET /v1/tenants/{tenantId}/orders/{orderId}` | `orders:read` | no | 2000ms |
| `getOrderV2` | `GET /v2/tenants/{tenantId}/orders/{orderId}` | `orders:read` | no | 2000ms |

Send an `Idempotency-Key` with every idempotent call. Retrying with the same key does not repeat the effect; retrying without one does.

⚠️ `getOrder` is deprecated since 2026-09-01 and stops answering on 2027-12-31; move to `getOrderV2`.

### `placeOrder`

`POST /v1/tenants/{tenantId}/orders`

Request:

| field | type |
| --- | --- |
| `tenantId` | uuid |
| `customerId` | uuid |
| `customerEmail` | string |
| `total` | money |

Response:

| field | type |
| --- | --- |
| `orderId` | uuid |

Declared failures, as `application/problem+json` (RFC 7807):

| status | code | retriable | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 422 | `order_rejected` | **no** | the order does not pass the rules |

Match on `code`, not on the status or the prose: the code is part of this contract and the other two are not. A failure marked not retriable will not end differently the second time.

## Events you can subscribe to

Subscribe instead of polling. Every message carries the CloudEvents envelope: `traceparent`, `correlationId` and `causationId`, so what you do with it stays attached to what caused it.

### `order.placed@v1`

| field | type |
| --- | --- |
| `orderId` | uuid |
| `customerId` | uuid |
| `customerEmail` | string |
| `total` | money |

The version is in the name. A change that breaks you arrives as a new `@vN`, not as a new field on this one.

## What it guarantees

Reads are eventually consistent: what you just wrote may not be in the next read. Under a partition it degrades and keeps answering with what it has, up to 3000ms stale.

Personal data, declared: `customer_email`. It is redacted from this service's logs; what you do with it on your side is your declaration to make.

It calls `payments` to do its work: a failure there shows up here.
